why: Opening Library to back up a damaged recovered draft must not replace that original, and the suggested Save a copy action must be visible in the current workspace.
baseline: The added public Library regression failed on the prior editor: the implicit save rewrote the damaged original before backup. Retained assertion excerpt is baseline-failure.txt.
changes: Implicit saves keep recovered draft edits and view in a separate session checkpoint while preserving the damaged durable record.
Explicit Save and Ctrl/Cmd+S acknowledge replacement; their pending request cannot be coalesced into an implicit recovery request.
Session-recovery quota errors and concurrent edits stop navigation.
A directly visible Save a copy action appears beside recovered/conflicted status. Normal saves retain their existing durable path.
verified: Exact damaged record retained before and after Library, background saves and reload.
Actual original-record download preserves the JSON-serializable current and previous record.
Recovered title edits survive session reload without replacing the damaged original.
Injected session-recovery quota blocks navigation and keeps the current edits.
Explicit button and keyboard Save replace the original once.
Concurrent remote save is preserved; visible Save a copy creates an independent draft with local edits.
Incomplete current draft and unsupported cached draft handling remain intact.
Normal committed/lost worker replies, quota rollback, export/retry, reload/Undo and ordinary view-only recovery pass in separate final runs.
visualReview: Recovered and conflicted 1600x1000 desktop captures individually inspected. Status and Save a copy fit in the header and remain available in the Land workspace.
limits: Controlled unsupported-schema, session quota and remote-write cases; not physical corruption, disk failure or every crash/write phase.
Session recovery is scoped to the browser session; durable preservation requires explicit Save, Save a copy or exported backup.
Concurrent initial test runs hit rendering timeouts; the final retained runs were executed separately and all completed successfully.
The complete original builder objective and remaining release gates are unchanged.
